# Verdict: BROKEN as stated. The part that survives is "never mirror ICD-11"; the part that fails is "not before a source or reader names one" — and the verification clause it rests on is false in code today.

Disclosure first: my one `add-medical --dry-run` probe copied the DB to the session scratchpad and deleted it. Canonical `data/guidebook.db` is byte-identical to HEAD (`f257a0a5…`, verified). The brief said create nothing; I created and removed one file.

## The measurements — re-derived from the zip, in memory

| Claim | Re-derived | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| 36,044 entities · 28 ch · 1,353 blocks · 34,663 cats | 36,044 rows; chapter 28 / block 1,353 / category 34,663 | yes |
| 272 depth-1 blocks | 272 | yes |
| 108 depth-1 blocks in ch 06/08/09/10/11/15/21/22 | 108 (20+18+11+6+15+4+16+18) | yes |

| 6.4× / 4.7× | 108/17 = 6.35, 108/23 = 4.70 | yes |
| MB5 = 32 categories, ancestry MB4→MB4→MB5 | 32; `BlockL1-MB4 → BlockL2-MB4 → BlockL3-MB5` | yes |
| one source names a diagnosis (REF-00973), one partial (REF-00975), seven device/diagnosis-free | true of the 9 rows in **canonical** `evidence_sources` | yes, but see finding 6.2 |
| AX-COG-L is the only orphan axis; 24 distinct b-codes | both confirmed from `axes` / `population_axis_map` | yes |

Every figure reproduces. The argument breaks elsewhere.

## Six things nobody caught (attack 6 first, because it changes the rest)

**6.1 The writer cannot verify an anchor against the artefact it was built for.** `scripts/db.py:3271-3272` reads the payload's raw bytes and substring-matches the code. The only persisted WHO artefact is a deflate-compressed zip; `MB5`, `MB56`, `MB57`, `BlockL3-MB5`, `MG30`, `6A02` — none occur in its raw bytes. Confirmed by dry-run: `add-medical --icd11 BlockL3-MB5,MB56 --icd11-payload …/b92212138c67738a.zip` → `REFUSING: --icd11-payload does not contain ['BlockL3-MB5', 'MB56']`. So `ICD11-VERIFIED.md:53-54` ("payload check greps the artefact for the literal string… Nothing needs changing") and `:75` ("Unblocked: every anchor can be verified offline") are false, and the ruling's own operative clause at `references/project-standards.md:2970-2971` ("verified against the persisted release file at write time") is currently unexecutable. The MB5 verification at 02:47 was done by hand in Python, never through the writer. This is the claim the orchestrator was most confident about ("I was wrong — ICD-11 verifies", commit `6360a22`). Fix is small: either `insert_medical` opens zip members, or a member is extracted and persisted with a manifest line — the second is cleaner because it keeps "bytes on disk contain the code" literally true.

**6.2 The demand count omitted the session's own admissions.** The scratch `walk.db` (session scratchpad `batch06/walk.db`, 23:33, schema 73) holds **11** sources: REF-00979 Chow 2009, *"…for Young Men With Paraplegia"* — MB56 in the title — and REF-00980 Sanford 1997, *"People with Mobility Impairments"*. The "exactly one" at `project-standards.md:2961` was true of canonical and false of the corpus the same session was building four hours earlier. Two of eleven name a diagnosis needing MB5. The demand test would already be firing.

**6.3 "The eight chapters that could touch any of our 17 axes" is falsified by `axes` itself.** AX-CHM declares b435 (immunological) and b440 (respiration) → chapters 04 and 12; AX-CNT declares b620 (urination) and b525 (defecation) → chapters 16 and 13. None of 04/12/13/16 is in the eight. See attack 2.

**6.4 The grain the 108 was measured at is not the grain of the owner's example.** `BlockL3-MB5` is depth **3**; `BlockL3-MG3` (Pain) is depth 3. Depth-1 in ch 21 is `BlockL1-MB4` — "Symptoms… of the nervous system", which lumps paralysis with dizziness, headache, smell/taste and dyssomnia. In the eight chapters: 108 depth-1, 85 depth-2, 14 depth-3. "Block grain" is three grains, and the ruling never says which. At depth-1, `6A0` Neurodevelopmental holds 6A00 intellectual development, 6A01 language, 6A02 autism and 6A05 ADHD in one row — which destroys the AX-COG-L argument that the ledger cites as the lens's strongest case.

**6.5 A dangling artefact in three homes.** `decisions/DR-2026-09-11-…md:60`, `data/decisions/decision_register.yaml:6319` and the committed `decisions` row (migration `data_20260911012015…`, immutable) all cite `scratchpad/pr-134-repository-orientation/ADJUDICATION.md`. It was never committed; `git log --all` has no such path. The content survives only in `transcripts/harness_94859b50/subagents/2026-09-11T00-54-46_other_a382a8ba.jsonl` (search `Ruling 1.1`). The brief inherited the same wrong path.

**6.6 The sweep (`b3eaf7b`) missed a live prose caller.** `scripts/audit/medical_lens_integrity.py:99-100` still prints "the vocabulary's CONTENT is blocked on licensing (DG-NON item 7)" on every zero-row run — the exact text the commit says it corrected in the registry. Rule 4, unswept. Also: the PR body says "A data migration is applied; the specification stage is writable for the first time" — canonical `base_parameters` = 0 and no migration inserts into it. That sentence describes scratch state.

## Attack 1 — principled design or rationalisation? Rationalisation, on the trigger clause.

The owner's four verbatim messages (main transcript): *"Ensure that medical gets filled out."* (00:52) · *"Yes, use ICD-11. eg MB5 series…"* (02:28) · *"maybe the medical vocabulary is just too granular to be usable."* (03:42). The first is an instruction; the third is a doubt about **grain**, not about **whether**. The ledger at `:2948` converts the doubt into a ruling that yields zero rows — which is `ORDER-OF-WORK.md:97` ("stays empty; explicitly deferred") re-instated under a new name, six hours after the owner overruled it.

The "reader's query" trigger (`:2970`) is unreachable: pre-launch, there is no reader, no query log, no mechanism. So the only live trigger is admitted sources, and the answer to "when does a reader with paraplegia get a route" is "when circulation-geometry research happens to say paraplegia" — which, per 6.2, it already has, and the session did not notice.

**What the owner actually asked for is a third design neither considered:** *"how it corresponds to OUR EXISTING ICF/identities/access needs on a high level"* — correspondence populated **from our side**. Our vocabulary is 17 axes + 23 populations, of which BAR, LPA, TALL, NDV, MOB, COM, ALL are identity-first or umbrella and take no anchor (`functional-taxonomy.md:241-245`). The bounded set is roughly 15–20 rows, not 108 and not zero, and the project's own §4 table already names the anchors for several (`:293` AUT 6A02, `:294` ADHD 6A05, `:304` LCOV RA02). §8's "name what reads it" is satisfied — the reader is the lens switch D-0170 was ruled for. Under this design the SCI→MB5/MB57 row is the first row either way; the difference is that the 22 other communities get their route now rather than when a paper mentions them.

**Ruling: keep "never mirror the classification"; strike "not before a source or reader names it"; replace with "populated by correspondence from the existing identity and axis registries, at the grain the owner's example uses (the block whose title states the functional presentation), plus on demand thereafter."** Content is DG-NON item 2 territory, but D-0188 clause 3 already instructs it.

## Attack 2 — the eight-chapter restriction understates, and its stated basis is wrong

Adding only the chapters the axes' own b-anchors reach (04, 12, 13, 16) gives 144 depth-1; adding 05, 20 (LPA/LMB anomalies) and V (WHODAS functioning) gives ~154; X (extension codes, 16,841 categories) is rightly excluded as post-coordination, not diagnosis. The direction of error strengthens "too granular to mirror" — but the framing "chapters that could touch any of our 17 axes" was derived from identities, not from the anchors it cites. Say: **understates; conclusion unaffected; premise false.**

## Attack 3 — "device-based literature" is about this project's queries, not the field

All 9 canonical sources are on one slug (`source_slug_links`), from one session. Of batch 05's 15 `search_executions`, 9 are device-framed (wheelchair / scooter / walking aid / Rollstuhl / 車椅子), and those 9 produced all 7 admissions; the person-framed Co-1/Co-2 legs admitted 2. A device-framed query returns device-framed papers. Batch 06's first backward-mining leg immediately produced a diagnosis-titled paper. And the acoustic/sensory slugs (28 executions from batches 01–03) would name hearing loss, autism, dementia by construction. **Does not generalise.** The proposed "finding for the book" (`:2984-2988`) should not ship as a finding about circulation literature.

## Attack 4 — chapter 21 over 08: wrong as a blanket rule, right as a selection rule

| Axis | ch21 candidate | disease-chapter candidate | Better |
|---|---|---|---|
| AX-AMB (b770, b730) | MB44 Abnormalities of gait and mobility; MB5 | 8A0 Movement disorders, 8B4, 8D2 | **ch21** — MB44 is b770 in WHO's words |
| AX-PAI (b280) | MG30 Chronic pain (depth-3 block MG3) | 8A8 Headache only | **ch21** — WHO put chronic pain here deliberately |
| AX-VIS-L/N (b210) | MC1 = red eye, floaters, discharge | **9D9 Vision impairment** (9D90.1–.6 severity grades) | **ch09** — the disease chapter holds the functional block |
| AX-AUD (b230) | MC4 = plugged ear, tinnitus | **AB5 Disorders with hearing impairment** | **ch10** |
| AX-COG-L (b117, b167) | MB21 cognition symptoms | 6A00 / 6A01 | **ch06** — a reader with "intellectual disability" holds 6A00 |
| AX-STA / COM | MG22 Fatigue | 8E49 Postviral fatigue, 8D89.2 POTS | **ch08** for COM's own conditions |

Rule that survives: **anchor on the block whose title states the presentation**, wherever it sits. Chapter 21 wins for motor and pain; the disease chapters win for sensory, cognitive and energy-limiting. ICD11-VERIFIED.md's "chapter 21 is the right chapter" should be narrowed to that.

No code, view or check derives `identity_medical_map` from `icf_medical_map ⋈ population_axis_map` (grep: only `dbcore.py:553-554` and the writer touch these tables; no view joins them). Under D-0184 the render is a column, so the traversal never renders. The trap therefore only bites a human authoring by join. A mechanical guard needs a "why is TALL on AX-REA" signal, and the schema holds it only as free text (`population_axis_map.note` = 'headroom/envelope'). No cheap gate has a semantic subject. §8's bar is not met; **do not build one.** The one honest addition is a rule, not a check: an `identity_medical_map` row is authored per identity, never generated — and the `relationship` CHECK already forces the wrong row to declare itself `identity_first` (navigation only), which is the schema's own prune.
